about: A faithful-feeling recreation of the start of Zork II. You start in a barrow, then cross a cavern and ravine to a formal garden with a gazebo. A wizard pops in to curse you, and a unicorn wanders through.

done.why: I'd had a short taste of the opening area and the oddball commands weren't getting anywhere, so I left after about 20 turns.

moments.note: The Wizard appears, waves his wand and makes me drop the sword.
The lamp answered 'I don't think that the lamp would agree with you' when I tried to eat it.
Many odd commands like 'attack the darkness with the sword' or 'smell the roses' got only 'You can't see any such thing.'

wished: Smell the roses, or have the unicorn react to the glowing sword.

lines.line: For a change, you look before leaping. You realize you would never survive.
lines.why: A good refusal with some personality.
A funny reply to my attempt to light the lantern with the sword.

fun.why: Charming but I only played briefly.

engagement.why: Easy to move through, but nothing pulled me on.

difficulty.why: Nothing blocked me in this stretch.

interestingness.why: The setting is familiar and the wizard's interruption was a nice touch.

prose.why: Clear and evocative room descriptions and good refusal lines.
